'''''Alopecurus myosuroides''''' is an [[Annual plant|annual]] [[Poaceae|grass]], native to [[Eurasia]], found in moist meadows, [[Deciduous|deciduous forests]], and on cultivated and waste land.<ref name=":0" /> It is also known as '''slender meadow foxtail''', '''black-grass''', '''twitch grass''', and '''black twitch'''.

==Description==
It can grow up to 80 cm high, often growing in tufts. The leaves are hairless. Leaf sheath is smooth, green to purplish in colour.  The leaf blade is pointed, 3 to 16 cm long and 2-8 millimeters wide, green, rough in texture.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=Riches|first=Charles|date=November 19, 2019|title=Alopecurus myosuroides (black-grass)|url=https://www.cabi.org/isc/datasheet/4360#todescription|url-status=live|access-date=April 29, 2021|website=CABI Invasive Species Compendium|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160716201615/http://www.cabi.org/isc/datasheet/4360 |archive-date=2016-07-16 }}</ref> The [[spikelet]]s are cylindrical, yellow-green, pale green or purple in colour, and may be 1-12 centimeters long.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Naylor|first=Robert E. L.|date=1972|title=Alopecurus Myosuroides Huds. (A. Agrestis L.)|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2258364|journal=Journal of Ecology|volume=60|issue=2|pages=611–622|doi=10.2307/2258364|jstor=2258364 |bibcode=1972JEcol..60..611N |issn=0022-0477|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

It flowers from May to August.<ref>''Grasses'' by C E Hubbard, 1978, published by Penguin Books</ref>

==Weed status==
In the UK, where it is known to farmers as black-grass, it is a major [[weed]] of [[cereal]] crops as it produces a large amount of seed which is shed before the crop is cut. It has developed [[Pesticide resistance|resistance]] to a range of [[herbicides]] used to control it. [[Herbicide resistance]] testing is often needed to understand what herbicides will be effective at treating it.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Burgos |first1=Nilda R. |last2=Tranel |first2=Patrick J. |last3=Streibig |first3=Jens C. |last4=Davis |first4=Vince M. |last5=Shaner |first5=Dale |last6=Norsworthy |first6=Jason K. |last7=Ritz |first7=Christian |title=Review: Confirmation of Resistance to Herbicides and Evaluation of Resistance Levels |journal=Weed Science |date=March 2013 |volume=61 |issue=1 |pages=4–20 |doi=10.1614/WS-D-12-00032.1|doi-access=free }}</ref> It can occur at very high densities, competing with the crop and seriously reducing the yield of crops such as [[wheat]] and [[barley]] if not controlled.

The seeds have a short period of dormancy and viability, and the numbers may be reduced by surface cultivation after harvest.
